content.title: A pure-Go HTML to PDF converter
content.lede: gowkhtmltopdf is a clean-room, pure-Go work-alike for wkhtmltopdf that turns server-generated HTML into multi-page PDFs and images. It is built for controlled reports: invoices, statements, tables, and documents with headers, footers, TOCs, and PDF outlines.

items.title: MVP v0.1.0
items.body: Phases 0-9 of the canonical plan are implemented: load, parse, style, layout, paginate, paint, and PDF 1.4 write, plus PNG/JPEG image mode. The `VERSION` file is the single source of truth; an unstamped build reports the `0.1.0-dev` fallback via `--version`.

items.title: Deterministic output
items.body: Identical input bytes produce identical PDF bytes on every run. The 10-page invoice gate (10 sections by 40 rows, repeated `<thead>`) outputs 96,341 bytes byte-identical each run, with a generous CI budget of under 5 s.

items.title: Two static binaries
items.body: `gowkhtmltopdf` (PDF) and `gowkhtmltoimage` (PNG/JPEG) build with `CGO_ENABLED=0` into statically linked ELF/Mach-O executables with no native runtime library requirements. The first build may download the allowlisted pure-Go module graph; later builds can run offline with the cache populated.

items.title: MIT licensed
items.body: MIT License, Copyright (c) 2026 Chinmay Sawant. This is an independent reimplementation: the project does not link to or redistribute wkhtmltopdf, Qt, or WebKit (wkhtmltopdf itself is LGPL).

sections.heading: Clean-room rewrite
sections.body: This codebase is not a binding to wkhtmltopdf/Qt/WebKit and not a wrapper around any commercial HTML-to-PDF API. The full pipeline (load, parse, CSS, layout, paginate, paint, PDF write) is implemented in this repository.

sections.heading: Pure-Go runtime boundary
sections.body: Runtime code uses the Go standard library plus two allowlisted pure-Go direct modules: `github.com/go-text/typesetting` for OpenType shaping and `github.com/tdewolff/canvas` for SVG rasterization. There are no third-party PDF/HTML/CSS APIs, no Chrome/WebKit embedding, and no cgo. Retain upstream notices for these dependencies and bundled fonts when preparing a redistribution archive.

sections.heading: AI-assisted development
sections.body: Plans and architecture came from Grok 4.5: phase ledgers under `plans/`, the scope freeze, feasibility, and the execution map. DeepSeek drove roughly 90% of the bulk implementation (settings/CLI, loader, PDF writer, HTML/CSS/layout, pagination, header/footer and TOC, image mode, library API, hardening).
bullets: Last-mile correctness (roughly 10%) was handed to Grok 4.5 with a concrete gate: run `make samples`, fix whatever fails, and open the generated PDFs.
Early DeepSeek output could emit PDF files, but they were not reliably workable in real viewers: empty or malformed catalogs, wrong stream compression, broken font advances.
The final pass closed that gap: Flate/zlib streams, Catalog outlines, CLI page-scoped flags, glyph `/Widths` on a 1000-unit em, and Latin-1 text encoding.
Letter-spacing is fixed for Latin text; complex pages such as full Wikipedia articles still need follow-up for Unicode/CID fonts and richer CSS.

sections.heading: The OSS story
sections.body: gowkhtmltopdf is MIT licensed under Chinmay Sawant and requires Go 1.26+. It is an independent clean-room reimplementation of the wkhtmltopdf CLI and behavior, so it shares none of wkhtmltopdf's LGPL obligations and does not ship Qt or WebKit. A direct CLI comparison against wkhtmltopdf 0.12.6.1 (2026-08-09) shows gowkhtmltopdf faster and lower-RSS at every tested size from 2 to 500 pages.

content.title: Scope boundary: a report engine, not a browser
content.body: gowkhtmltopdf converts server-generated HTML into multi-page PDFs without a browser process. There is no JavaScript, CSS support is a documented subset (flex, grid, and positioning are partial), and pixel parity with Chrome or WebKit is not a goal. Use it for invoices, statements, tables, and multi-page documents with headers, footers, TOCs, and PDF outlines.
